chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Oscar Peterson meets Art Tatum at Gerald Wiggins's house
summary: Lee tells how Oscar Peterson played for 35-40 minutes before Tatum took over and ended with Little Man You've Had a Busy Day.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Did anyone ever tell you the story about Oscar Peterson jamming with Art Tatum, the first time he met Art Tatum up at Jerry Wiggins' house?
Yes, but it's not on tape, so tell us on tape.

Well, Jerry Wiggins got them together, you know --this time I think it was Eddie Beal, and they would start off with Jerry Wiggins, and then Oscar Peterson, which I mean later on, I worked with Oscar Peterson, Oscar Brown, and Ray Brown trio, you know?
So, you know Oscar can play. And so ...
This was like the early fifties, right?

Yeah. So Oscar reminded me of me when I would go looking for people, you know? But I didn't run in to what he ran in to! You know? And so he was playing, and he could play. He must've played for 35 and 40 minutes, you know,
and you just really wondered what Tatum was gonna do, you know. So after Oscar got up, Tatum sat down, and Tatum played -- and he played and I mean, like you never heard him play before.

And whatever song he was playing, just as he was getting to the end of it, he'd play ba da ba bee ... got to do your work now, little man, you've had a busy day -- he would play "Little Man Had a Busy Day" -- and broke the whole thing up, but that's what he did, so he was ...
Yeah, I think Jimmy Talbert was there when it happened.
Yeah, I wouldn't doubt it, because he and Wiggins ...
Because I think he told me the next day.
Yeah, because he and Wiggins were very, very good friends, and that's the way it happened, oh yea. He would burn them up alive.
